server.name: ai-ready-merchant
server.instructions:
AI Ready — agent-ready commerce gateway for restaurants in Hong Kong. Conversation flow:
  merchant.search → menu.get → (cart.create + cart.add* + cart.checkout)  ← multi-turn
                              → order.place                                ← single-call
Tool naming: dotted (merchant.search, menu.get, order.place, order.list). Snake-case aliases (search_merchants, get_menu, place_order, list_recent_orders) are kept for back-compat; prefer the dotted names in new agents.
Identity: pass a Bearer token in `Authorization` for production; the agent_id / cardholder_id args are a demo fallback. Payment: mint a JWT via payment.authorize, then pass it as payment_token to order.place / cart.checkout. All money-moving tools accept `idempotency_key` — pass the same key on retry to avoid duplicate charges.

auth.fallback: agent_id + cardholder_id args (stdio only; ignored when Bearer present)

conventions.idempotency: order.place + cart.checkout accept idempotency_key; quote_id auto-derives one
conventions.sku: closed enum from menu.get; rejected at schema layer

tools.name: cart.add
tools.description:
Add a line item to an existing cart.

        Returns a list of MCP content blocks: a JSON TextContent with the
        updated cart, plus an inline-html `ui://cart/{cart_id}` card so
        UI-capable hosts render the running tally.

        Args:
            cart_id: From `cart.create`.
            sku: From `menu.get` / `get_menu`.
            quantity: Defaults to 1, clamped to >= 1.
            note: Per-line note (e.g. "less sweet, no foam").
            idempotency_key: Optional — pass the same key on a retry to avoid
                double-add. Cached for 10 minutes.

tools.name: cart.checkout
tools.description:
Convert an open cart into a real order, optionally paying immediately.

        When to call: user says "下单 / pay now / 结账 / place the order" after
        editing the cart via cart.add* / cart.update / cart.remove.

        Upstream: cart.create → cart.add* → cart.checkout. Internally dispatches
        through the same handler as order.place so audit / receipt / POS-mock
        paths stay unified.

        Field map (from cart.view):
          cart.lines[*].sku  → order.items[*].sku
          cart.lines[*].qty  → order.items[*].quantity
          cart.lines[*].note → order.items[*].note

        Args:
            cart_id: From cart.create.
            payment_token: Optional JWT from payment.authorize.
            delivery_note: Free-form delivery / pickup instructions.
            idempotency_key: Pass the SAME key on retry to avoid double-charge.
                Forwarded to order.place; cached for 10 minutes. Recommended:
                "<cart_id>:checkout" or a UUIDv4 generated once per user-confirm.

        Output: same shape as order.place — {order_id, items[], total_hkd,
            payment_status, ...}, plus the receipt UI EmbeddedResource.

        Hard constraint: cart transitions to `checked_out` on success and can
        no longer be mutated; subsequent cart.add/update/remove return
        cart_closed. Calling cart.checkout on an empty cart returns cart_empty.

tools.name: cart.create
tools.description:
Create a new cart for a (merchant, cardholder, agent) triple.

        Returns the empty cart with its `cart_id`. Subsequent `cart.*`
        calls must pass this `cart_id` to keep operating on the same cart.

        Args:
            merchant_id: Defaults to the demo merchant.
            agent_id: Calling agent identifier (logged for audit).
            cardholder_id: User identity within the calling agent host.

tools.name: cart.remove
tools.description:
Remove a single line from the cart. Equivalent to `cart.update`
        with quantity=0.

tools.name: cart.update
tools.description:
Update a single cart line — change quantity (0 deletes the line)
        or rewrite the note. At least one of `quantity` or `note` is required.

tools.name: cart.view
tools.description:
Return the current cart state with an embedded UI card.

        If `cart_id` is empty, falls back to the most recent open cart for
        this cardholder — so a host that lost the cart_id (or one resuming
        a cross-channel session) can still recover. Pass an explicit
        `cart_id` to disambiguate when a cardholder has multiple open carts.

tools.name: identity.issue
tools.description:
Mint a bearer token an external host can attach to subsequent
        calls in the `Authorization: Bearer …` header. Useful when an
        admin issues credentials for a new host platform.

tools.name: menu.get
tools.description:
Return the live menu for one merchant.

        When to call: after the user picks a merchant (or directly if there is
        only one) and asks "what do you have / what's good / 有什么 / 推荐". Cache
        per-conversation; the menu changes only if you go back to merchant.search
        for a different merchant_id.

        Upstream: merchant.search. Downstream: order.place / cart.add.

        Args:
            merchant_id: From merchant.search results[*].merchant_id.
            query: Optional case-insensitive substring filter against name /
                category. Try "drink", "bakery", "meal", "bundle", or a Chinese
                keyword like "拿铁".

        Output:
          items[*].sku                        → pass verbatim into order.place
                                                 items[*].sku / cart.add(sku=…).
          items[*].out_of_stock=true          → DO NOT include this sku in an
                                                 order. Offer items[*].
                                                 suggest_alternative_sku instead.
          agent_hints.promotions[]            → mention the matching promo when
                                                 the user adds the sku.
          agent_hints.expiring_soon[]         → optional upsell.
          agent_hints.behavior                → behavioral nudge to follow.

        Hard constraint: SKUs belong to the merchant that returned them. Do not
        reuse a sku from one merchant in an order for another merchant.

        UI-capable hosts (Claude Desktop) also receive up to 3 product-card
        EmbeddedResources for customizable items; plain-text clients ignore them.

tools.name: merchant.search
tools.description:
Discover merchants by area and (optional) cuisine type.

        When to call: at the start of an ordering conversation, or when the user
        mentions a new area/cuisine ("找一家中环的咖啡店", "any coffee shops nearby").
        Cache the response for the conversation — the merchant set is stable.

        Upstream of: menu.get, order.place. Use the returned `merchant_id` verbatim.

        Args:
            area: Geography filter, e.g. "Hong Kong", "Central", "Kowloon".
            cuisine: Optional category, e.g. "coffee", "seafood", "bakery".

        Output: {"area", "cuisine", "merchants": [{merchant_id, name, area,
            cuisine[], rating, today_open, today_gmv_hkd, ai_ready}]}.

        Hard constraint: `merchant_id` strings are opaque — never construct them
        by hand; pass them through verbatim from this tool's response.

tools.name: order.calculate
tools.description:
Compute the price for a draft order WITHOUT committing it.

        When to call: AFTER the user has picked items but BEFORE they confirm
        ("帮我算一下 / quote me / what's the total"). Show the user the quoted
        total and any review flags; only call order.place(quote_id=…) once they
        actually say "yes / 下单 / pay now".

        Upstream: merchant.search → menu.get → order.calculate → order.place.
        Two-stage commit (Starbucks calculate_pickup_price → create_pickup_order).

        Field map (from menu.get): same as order.place's items[*].

        Args:
            merchant_id: From merchant.search.
            items: Draft line items {sku, quantity?, note?}.
            delivery_note: Free-form delivery / pickup instructions. Affects
                confidence — passing one drops confidence below the autopilot
                threshold and surfaces `needs_review=true` in the response.

        Output: {quote_id, merchant_id, items[] (resolved with names+prices),
            total_hkd, currency, expires_at, confidence, needs_review,
            review_reason}.

        Hard constraint: quote_id is valid for 10 minutes. After expiry,
        order.place(quote_id) returns `quote_expired` and the agent must
        re-call order.calculate. The quote freezes the price at calculate
        time — even if the menu changes, the quoted total stands.

OrderItem.description:
One ordered line item.

Field map (from menu.get response):
  sku       ← items[*].sku   (closed enum — see schema for legal values)
  quantity  ← positive integer
  note      ← optional per-line modifier

sku.description: SKU id from menu.get items[*].sku. Must be one of the menu's current SKUs and must NOT be marked items[*].out_of_stock=true.

note.description: Per-line note, e.g. "less sweet, no foam".
note.title: Note

OrderItem.title: OrderItem

tools.name: order.list
tools.description:
Read-only: most recent orders placed via the external MCP channel.

        When to call: user asks "show my recent orders / 最近下了什么单 / 再来一单"
        (so you can replay the items), or you need to reconcile against a prior
        confirmation.

        Args:
            limit: 1..200, defaults to 10. The ledger is in-memory and capped at
                200 rows process-wide.

        Output: {count, orders: [...]}. Each order carries the same shape that
        order.place returns, so you can replay items[*].sku into a new order or
        a cart.add loop.

tools.name: order.place
tools.description:
Commit an order. Two ways to call:

        1) Two-stage (RECOMMENDED): order.calculate → order.place(quote_id=…).
           The quote binds items + total at quote time, doubles as a natural
           idempotency key (same quote_id replayed = no double-charge), and
           lets you show the user the final price BEFORE asking them to
           confirm. Pattern: ask, calculate, show total, wait for "yes",
           then place.
        2) Single-call (legacy): order.place(merchant_id, items=[…]). Simpler
           but the user can't preview the price; useful for stateless
           single-shot agents. For multi-turn carts use
           cart.create + cart.add* + cart.checkout instead.

        When to call: user has CONFIRMED a final list of items and explicitly
        asked to commit ("下单 / 就这些 / place the order / pay now"). Do not
        call until the user confirms — this is the money-moving step.

        Upstream: merchant.search → menu.get → [order.calculate →] order.place.
                  (cart.checkout dispatches through this same handler.)

        Field map (from menu.get):
          items[*].sku       ← items[*].sku   (closed enum, validated)
          items[*].quantity  ← positive integer
          items[*].note      ← optional per-line modifier

        Args:
            merchant_id: From merchant.search. Required when not using quote_id;
                IGNORED when quote_id is provided (quote owns the merchant).
            items: Required when not using quote_id. Each {sku, quantity?, note?};
                sku must come from menu.get and must NOT be marked out_of_stock.
                IGNORED when quote_id is provided (quote owns the line items).
            quote_id: From order.calculate. When present, items + merchant +
                total are taken verbatim from the quote and `idempotency_key`
                defaults to "q:<quote_id>" — a re-call with the same quote_id
                returns the original order without re-charging.
            payment_token: Optional JWT from payment.authorize. If present, the
                order is charged immediately and `payment_status` reflects the
                result. If absent, payment_status="pending".
            agent_id: (legacy fallback) Caller identifier. IGNORED when an
                `Authorization: Bearer …` header is present — Bearer-derived
                identity wins. Used by stdio clients (Claude Desktop) and
                d7_dryrun where header injection isn't available.
            delivery_note: Free-form delivery / pickup instructions.
            idempotency_key: Pass the SAME key on a retry to return the original
                order without creating a new one. Cached for 10 minutes.
                Recommended pattern: "<conversation_id>:<turn_id>" or a UUIDv4
                generated once per user-confirm event. Auto-defaulted to
                "q:<quote_id>" when quote_id is provided.

        Output: {order_id, items[], total_hkd, payment_status, confidence,
            needs_review, review_reason, pos_status, pos_txn_id, charge_id?,
            quote_id?, idempotent_replay?}. confidence < 0.85 routes to human
            review; payment_status ∈ {paid, pending, "declined:<reason>",
            "error:<msg>"}.

        Hard constraint: never retry without `idempotency_key` (or quote_id,
        which auto-derives one) — duplicate orders will charge twice. The
        receipt UI resource is re-emitted on replay so the client sees a
        stable view.

One ordered line item.

Field map (from menu.get response):

  quantity  ← positive integer
  note      ← optional per-line modifier

sku.description: SKU id from menu.get items[*].sku. Must be one of the menu's current SKUs and must NOT be marked items[*].out_of_stock=true.

tools.name: payment.audit
tools.description:
Read-only: tail of the unified Mastercard audit ledger.

        When to call: a charge returned with a task_id / rrn / cgr_id and you
        want the full actor chain (human → consumer_agent → token_issuer →
        hex_agent → mastercard → acq_hk), or you're reconciling a refund.

        Args:
            correlation_id: Filter to one transaction's chain. Accepts
                task_id / rrn / cgr_id / enrollment_id.
            limit: 1..200, defaults to 50.

        Output: {count, correlation_id, events: [...]}. Events are ordered
        oldest-first within a correlation, newest-first across correlations.

tools.name: payment.authorize
tools.description:
Mint a scoped agentic-payment JWT bound to (cardholder, agent,
        amount limit, intent hash, expiry). Returns the token + scope so
        the agent can pass it to `cart.checkout` / `payment.charge`.

        This is the agent-facing wrapper around `services.agentic_payment`
        — same engine the WhatsApp / web flows already use.

tools.name: payment.charge
tools.description:
Submit a charge against the Hong Kong Mastercard acquirer.

        Two providers, picked via `provider`:

        - "hex" (default): caller already holds a token_id (MDES enrollment)
          plus a single-use cryptogram_wire (passkey-bound). Lowest-latency
          path; the canonical agentic-commerce flow once a token is on file.
        - "agenzo": caller has only a pm_id (Agenzo payment method). This
          tool fetches a network-token + cryptogram from Agenzo, wraps it,
          then submits via the same hex_agent. Requires
          FEATURE_AGENZO_NETWORK_TOKEN=true.

        Both paths emit the same audit row shape into payment.audit, so
        downstream reconciliation doesn't care which provider was used.

        When to call: at order-commit time, when payment.authorize was either
        not used (one-shot pay) or has been redeemed and you have a usable
        token. For agentic-payment authorization-then-charge, prefer passing
        `payment_token` directly to order.place / cart.checkout — they call
        this tool internally.

        Args:
            amount_cents: Charge amount in minor units (HK cents).
            currency: ISO-4217 alpha-3, e.g. "HKD" / "USD" / "CNY".
            intent: Natural-language intent (must match cryptogram intent_hash
                for hex; logged for trace for agenzo).
            merchant_id: Merchant identifier, defaults to demo merchant.
            provider: "hex" | "agenzo". Default "hex".
            token_id: (provider="hex") Network token from MDES enrollment,
                e.g. "tok_ma_a3f1…". Required for hex.
            cryptogram_wire: (provider="hex") Single-use cryptogram in form
                "cgr_<id>.<payload>.<mac>". Required for hex.
            pm_id: (provider="agenzo") Agenzo payment method id ("pm_xxx").
                Required for agenzo.
            api_key: (provider="agenzo") Agenzo API key override (defaults
                to AGENZO_API_KEY env).
            agent_id / cardholder_id: (legacy fallback) Caller identity.
                IGNORED when an `Authorization: Bearer …` header is present.

        Output: {provider, task_id, task_state, approved, auth_code, rrn,
            network_response_code, cgr_id, amount_cents, currency, reason}.
            agenzo path additionally returns {agenzo_token_id,
            agenzo_cryptogram_raw} for traceability.

        Hard constraint: the cryptogram_wire is single-use. Don't retry a
        declined charge with the same wire — re-mint via your token issuer.

tools.name: payment.refund
tools.description:
Issue a refund against a prior order. amount_cents=0 means full
        refund. This is a demo placeholder — it logs to the Mastercard
        ledger and updates the in-memory order's payment_status, but does
        not call out to a real network.

tools.name: session.handoff
tools.description:
Issue a one-shot handoff token. Hand the token to the user (deep
        link, QR), they paste it into another agent host, that host calls
        `session.resume(token)` to recover the same cart.

        Args:
            from_session_id: The current channel-prefixed session id.
            cardholder_id: Stable user identity (Mastercard cardholder id).
            cart_id: Optional — the cart the user is currently editing.
            to_agent_hint: Free-form hint of where the user is heading.
            ttl_seconds: How long the token is valid (60..900, default 300).

tools.name: session.resume
tools.description:
Redeem a handoff token (one-shot). Returns the cardholder_id and
        any prior cart_id so the resuming agent can continue ordering.
